To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
we have found a new way of calculating chiral condensate, quark number density, and quark number susceptibility, using a static quark source.
the correlations of chiral condensation and quark number density with static quark source have been studied using a 3-flavor staggered quark action at β=4.2 and 4.4.

(i) the chiral condensate, the quark number density and the quark number susceptibility are all correlated with the quark source, (ii) the quark source is correlated with the quarks’ momentum distribution, and (iii) the chiral order parameter and the quark momentum distribution are correlated with each other.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the properties of QCD matter under conditions that are expected to be realized in the cores of compact stars and in heavy ion collisions.
the study of the correlations of chiral condensation and quark number density fluctuations with static quark source.
the study of the correlations between chiral condensate and quark number density in the presence of static quark sources at finite density and temperature.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
the chiral condensate is not a good order parameter for QCD in the low temperature and high quark number density phase.
the chiral condensate is a good order parameter for the chiral phase transition in lattice QCD.
the quark condensates and densities are not correlated with the presence of a static quark source, but are strongly correlated with the gluonic condensates.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
we have found that the chiral condensate and quark number density are strongly correlated with the static quark potential in the confined phase.
the chiral condensate, quark number density, and the quark condensate are strongly correlated in the presence of a static quark source.
the chiral condensate is the dominant contribution to the static quark potential in the infrared regime.
The main takeaway from our work is that

the quark number susceptibilities and chiral condensate susceptibilities are not independent quantities, but are related by the same relations as in QCD, and therefore can be used as a consistency check for lattice QCD calculations of the quark number density.
the chiral condensate and the quark number density can be used to probe the phase structure of QCD at finite temperature and chemical potential.
the chiral condensate and the quark number density can be measured in lattice simulations with an accuracy that is not affected by the presence of a static quark.
